chunks: And it is narrated from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār that he said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: I am in the salat (prayer), and I feel a pain in my stomach, or rumbling, or throbbing. So he said: “Turn away and perform wudu (ablution), and build upon what has passed of your salat (prayer) so long as you have not invalidated the salat (prayer) by deliberate speech. But if you spoke forgetfully, then there is nothing upon you, and it is like one who spoke in the salat (prayer) forgetfully.”
I said: And if he turns his face away from the qiblah? He said: “Yes, even if he turns his face away from the qiblah.”

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the ritual act being discussed
key_terms.بِالْكَلَامِ: by speech, which can invalidate the prayer if deliberate
key_terms.غَمْزًا: a pain or pressing sensation felt in the stomach
key_terms.وَابْنِ: continue by building upon what has already been performed

ai.seo_question: If someone leaves salat (prayer) because of stomach discomfort and needs wudu (ablution), can they continue from where they left off?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for one who experiences abdominal disturbance during salat (prayer) and needs to leave in order to perform wudu (ablution). The Imam عليه السلام instructs that he may resume and build upon what has already passed of the prayer, provided he has not deliberately spoken; forgetful speech does not incur anything upon him. The ruling also applies even if he turns his face away from the qiblah.
